title: The Real Reason You Can't Tickle Yourself
hook: You cannot tickle yourself because your brain already knows what is coming.

narration.text: You cannot tickle yourself because your brain already knows what is coming.
When someone else tickles you, the sensation is unexpected.
Your brain's somatosensory cortex reacts strongly to this surprise.
But when you try to tickle yourself, your cerebellum sends a signal.
It predicts the exact touch sensation before it happens.
This prediction reduces the brain's response to the sensation.
The feeling is therefore not surprising, so it is not ticklish.
This predictive ability helps your brain distinguish self-generated actions.
It helps it filter out expected sensations from important new ones.
What other unexpected things has your brain learned to predict?

description: Ever wonder why you can't tickle yourself, no matter how hard you try? It all comes down to a fascinating trick your brain plays on itself. Learn how your brain's predictions change the way you feel touch.
